body: Hmm.. I think I know what the problem is, but I can't find the file I need.

Hi there! I'm new to contributing to Godot and got interested in this specific issue. After doing some research on it, I found that the current DPI (or perhaps PPI, to be a bit more precise, since what's actually being computed is hardware DPI) in the X11, Wayland, and Windows display server code is computed incorrectly, as it uses a different formula from the one that is considered correct and precise. This among other things results in different DPI values for horizontal and vertical display orientations.

After looking into the Godot repository a bit more, I noticed that this was actually fixed a long time ago for macOS in the already merged pull request #42477. In that PR, the initially incorrect formula was changed to the one that calculates the actual display PPI, rather than the average of horizontal and vertical PPIs, which is what's currently done in the X11, Wayland, and Windows implementations.

The correct implementation can be found on Wikipedia at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixel_density#:~:text=Calculation%20of%20monitor%20PPIedit.

Here's a comparison between the correct formula and the one currently used in Godot:

#### The correct formula is as follows (excerpt from Wikipedia):

PPI can be calculated from the screen's diagonal size in inches and the resolution in pixels (width and height). This can be done in two steps:

Calculate diagonal resolution in pixels using the Pythagorean theorem:
$`{\displaystyle d_{p}={\sqrt {w_{p}^{2}+h_{p}^{2}}}}`$

Calculate the PPI:
$`{\displaystyle PPI={\frac {d_{p}}{d_{i}}}}`$

where

$`{\displaystyle w_{p}}`$ is width resolution in pixels
$`{\displaystyle h_{p}}`$ is height resolution in pixels
$`{\displaystyle d_{p}}`$ is diagonal size in pixels.
$`{\displaystyle d_{i}}`$ is diagonal size in inches (this is the number advertised as the size of the display).

#### Whereas with the current implementation it is computed as the average of horizontal and vertical dpi's:

Calculate the horizontal DPI:
${\displaystyle d_{x} = \frac{w_p}{width_{mm}} \times 25.4}$

Calculate the vertical DPI:
${\displaystyle d_{y} = \frac{h_p}{height_{mm}} \times 25.4}$

Calculate the average DPI:
${\displaystyle DPI = \frac{d_{x} + d_{y}}{2}}$

where

${\displaystyle w_p}$ is width resolution in pixels  
${\displaystyle h_p}$ is height resolution in pixels  
${\displaystyle width_{mm}}$ is the physical width of the screen in millimeters  
${\displaystyle height_{mm}}$ is the physical height of the screen in millimeters

To be precise, here are the implementations I've found that currently use the averaging formula:
1. DisplayServerWindows::screen_get_dpi (platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp) - averaging formula
2. DisplayServerWayland::screen_get_dpi (platform/linuxbsd/wayland/display_server_wayland.cpp) - averaging formula
3. DisplayServerX11::screen_get_dpi (platform/linuxbsd/x11/display_server_x11.cpp) - averaging formula

The implementation for macOS, however, already uses the correct formula in the same method:

DisplayServerMacOS::screen_get_dpi (platform/macos/display_server_macos.mm) - correct formula, using Pythogoras theorem

I also thought that it would be useful to put the computation in some common function that could be called in all of these methods and that could be easily covered with a unit test.

So I wanted to ask: am I heading in the right direction, or are my findings perhaps incorrect? And if not, would it be possible for me to be assigned to this issue?

THX a lot in advance :)

@AThousandShips
